syllabus.head: Limits, Continuity & Differentiability
syllabus.text: Limits, indeterminate forms, continuity, and differentiability of single and multivariable functions.

syllabus.head: Mean Value Theorems
syllabus.text: Rolle's Theorem, Lagrange's Mean Value Theorem (LMVT), Cauchy's Mean Value Theorem (CMVT), and geometric/algebraic interpretations.

syllabus.head: Expansion of Functions
syllabus.text: Taylor's Theorem and Maclaurin's Theorem for functions of one variable, Taylor's Theorem for functions of two variables (multivariable Taylor expansions).

syllabus.head: Partial Differentiation
syllabus.text: Partial derivatives of first and higher orders, Euler's theorem on homogeneous functions, composite functions, total derivative, and change of variables in partial derivatives.

syllabus.head: Maxima and Minima
syllabus.text: Maxima and minima of functions of two and three variables, stationary points, saddle points, and Method of Lagrange Multipliers for constrained optimization.

parts.text: Verify Rolle's Theorem for the function f(x) = log ((x<sup>2</sup> + ab)/(x(a+b))) in the interval [a, b].
Discuss the applicability of Lagrange's Mean Value Theorem for the function f(x) = { 2 + x<sup>2</sup>, x ≤ 1 ; 3x, x > 1 } on [-1, 2].
Verify Rolle's Theorem for f(x) = (sin x)/e<sup>x</sup> (or e<sup>-x</sup> sin x) in [0, π].
Verify Mean Value Theorem for f(x) = x(x-1)(x-2) in [0, 1/2].
Verify Rolle's Theorem for the function f(x) = sin x + cos x - 1 in [0, π/2].
Find the value of c using Lagrange's Mean Value Theorem for f(x) = Ax<sup>2</sup> + Bx + C in [a, b], or for f(x) = 2x<sup>2</sup> + 3x + 4 in [1, 2].
Show that c of the Cauchy Mean Value Theorem for the interval (a, b) is the geometric mean of a and b if f(x) = √x and g(x) = 1/√x.

pyqs.title: Taylor's Series for Single and Two Variables

parts.text: Find the first six terms of the expansion of the function e<sup>x</sup> log(1+y) in a Taylor series in the neighborhood of the point (0, 0).
Expand sin x in powers of (x - π/2). Hence find the value of sin 91°, given 1° = 0.0174 rad.
State Taylor's theorem in two variables. Expand e<sup>x</sup> sin y in powers of x and y about (0, 0) up to third-degree terms.
Expand y<sup>x</sup> at (1, 1) up to the second-degree term by Taylor's Theorem.
Express x<sup>4</sup> + 3x<sup>3</sup> - 8x + 20 in powers of (x + 1) using Taylor's theorem.
Expand x<sup>2</sup> y + 3y - 2 in powers of (x - 1) and (y + 2) using Taylor's theorem.
Show that the function f(x) = { x sin(1/x), x ≠ 0 ; 0, x = 0 } is continuous but not differentiable at x = 0.
Find the values of a and b if lim<sub>x → 0</sub> (x(1 + a cos x) - b sin x)/x<sup>3</sup> = 1.
If x<sup>x</sup> y<sup>y</sup> z<sup>z</sup> = c, show that at x = y = z, (∂<sup>2</sup> z)/(∂x ∂y) = -(x log<sub>e</sub>(ex))<sup>-1</sup>.
If z = x log(x+r) - r, where x = r cos θ, y = r sin θ, prove that (∂<sup>2</sup> z)/(∂x<sup>2</sup>) + (∂<sup>2</sup> z)/(∂y<sup>2</sup>) = 1/(x+r).
If u = f(r) and x = r cos θ, y = r sin θ, prove that (∂<sup>2</sup> u)/(∂x<sup>2</sup>) + (∂<sup>2</sup> u)/(∂y<sup>2</sup>) = f''(r) + 1/rf'(r).

pyqs.title: Constrained Maxima & Minima via Lagrange Multipliers

parts.text: Find the minimum value of x<sup>2</sup> + y<sup>2</sup> + z<sup>2</sup>, given the constraint ax + by + cz = p.

If u = ax<sup>2</sup> + by<sup>2</sup> + cz<sup>2</sup> subject to x<sup>2</sup> + y<sup>2</sup> + z<sup>2</sup> = 1 and lx + my + nz = 0, prove that the stationary values of u satisfy the determinantal relation l<sup>2</sup>/(a-u) + m<sup>2</sup>/(b-u) + n<sup>2</sup>/(c-u) = 0.

Find the maximum and minimum distances of the point (3, 4, 12) or (1, 2, -1) from the sphere x<sup>2</sup> + y<sup>2</sup> + z<sup>2</sup> = 1 (or x<sup>2</sup> + y<sup>2</sup> + z<sup>2</sup> = 24) using Lagrange's method of multipliers.
The temperature T at any point (x, y, z) in space is T = 400xyz<sup>2</sup>. Find the highest temperature on the surface of the unit sphere x<sup>2</sup> + y<sup>2</sup> + z<sup>2</sup> = 1.
Divide 24 into three parts such that the continued product of the first, square of the second, and cube of the third is a maximum (f = x y<sup>2</sup> z<sup>3</sup> subject to x + y + z = 24).
Find the area of the greatest rectangle that can be inscribed in an ellipse x<sup>2</sup>/a<sup>2</sup> + y<sup>2</sup>/b<sup>2</sup> = 1.
Examine the function sin x + sin y + sin(x+y) for maximum and minimum values.

labs.title: 3D Surface Topography & Lagrange Multipliers Constraint Optimizer
points: Physical 3D Assets:
3D multivariable surface canvas plotting z = f(x, y) or 4D implicit isosurfaces (u = f(x, y, z)) as a semi-transparent topographical terrain.
3D intersecting constraint curve/plane (e.g., plane lx + my + nz = 0 intersecting sphere x<sup>2</sup> + y<sup>2</sup> + z<sup>2</sup> = 1) rendered as a bright red spatial path.
Interactive Controls:
Objective function selector: f(x, y, z) = x<sup>2</sup> + y<sup>2</sup> + z<sup>2</sup> vs. T = 400xyz<sup>2</sup> vs. u = ax<sup>2</sup> + by<sup>2</sup> + cz<sup>2</sup>.
External point coordinate drag-handles for distance minimization (e.g., (3, 4, 12) or (1, 2, -1)).
Multiplier slider (λ) balancing constraint gradients.

Gradient Alignment: At every point along the constraint curve, renders gradient vectors ∇f (blue) and ∇g (orange); visually locks when the vectors become parallel (∇f = λ∇g), identifying critical constrained stationary points.
Hessian Eigenvalue Matrix: Color-codes local critical points live: Green for local maxima, blue for local minima, and yellow for saddle points.

syllabus.head: Definite Integrals & Beta-Gamma Functions
syllabus.text: Definite integrals, properties, Beta and Gamma functions, fundamental relations (B(m, n) = (Γ(m)Γ(n))/(Γ(m+n)), Γ(1/2) = √π, Legendre's duplication formula), and definite integral evaluations.

syllabus.head: Curve Tracing
syllabus.text: Principles of tracing Cartesian, polar, and parametric curves (symmetry, origin, tangents, asymptotes, intercepts, nodal loops).

syllabus.head: Multiple Integrals
syllabus.text: Double and triple integrals, evaluation over Cartesian and polar domains, Dirichlet's integral for volume calculations.

syllabus.head: Change of Order & Coordinate Transformations
syllabus.text: Changing the order of integration in double integrals, transformation of variables (Cartesian to polar, cylindrical, and spherical coordinates).

parts.text: Prove that ∫<sub>0</sub><sup>1</sup> (x<sup>m-1</sup> + x<sup>n-1</sup>)/((1+x)<sup>m+n</sup>) dx = B(m, n).
Prove the relation B(m, n) = (Γ(m)Γ(n))/(Γ(m+n)) and show that Γ(1/2) = √π.
Evaluate the integral ∫<sub>0</sub><sup>2π</sup> sin<sup>4</sup>θ cos<sup>2</sup>θ dθ using Beta and Gamma functions.
Evaluate ∫<sub>0</sub><sup>∞</sup>(x<sup>4</sup> (1 + x<sup>5</sup>))/((1 + x)<sup>15</sup>) dx using properties of Beta functions.
Show that ∫<sub>0</sub><sup>1</sup> x<sup>2</sup>/(√(1 - x<sup>4</sup>)) dx × ∫<sub>0</sub><sup>1</sup> dx/(√(1 + x<sup>4</sup>)) = π/4√2.
Evaluate ∫<sub>0</sub><sup>∞</sup>e<sup>-x<sup>2</sup></sup> dx using Gamma functions.
Change the order of integration in ∫<sub>0</sub><sup>∞</sup>∫<sub>0</sub><sup>x</sup> x e<sup>-x<sup>2</sup> / y</sup> dy dx and evaluate it.
Evaluate the double integral ∫<sub>0</sub><sup>π</sup>∫<sub>x</sub><sup>π</sup>(sin y)/y dy dx by changing the order of integration.
Evaluate by changing the order of integration: ∫<sub>0</sub><sup>∞</sup>∫<sub>x</sub><sup>∞</sup>(e<sup>-y</sup>)/y dy dx.
Change the order of integration for ∫<sub>0</sub><sup>1</sup> ∫<sub>x<sup>2</sup></sub><sup>2-x</sup> xy dy dx and hence evaluate the integral.
Evaluate by changing the order of integration: ∫<sub>0</sub><sup>2a</sup> ∫<sub>x<sup>2</sup> / a</sub><sup>2a - x</sup> xy dy dx.
Solve ∫<sub>0</sub><sup>1</sup> ∫<sub>x</sub><sup>√(2 - x<sup>2</sup>)</sup> (x dy dx)/(√(x<sup>2</sup> + y<sup>2</sup>)) by changing the order of integration.

pyqs.title: Double & Triple Integration in Cartesian & Polar

parts.text: Change to polar coordinates and evaluate ∬(x<sup>2</sup> y<sup>2</sup>)/(x<sup>2</sup> + y<sup>2</sup>) dx dy over the annular region between concentric circles x<sup>2</sup> + y<sup>2</sup> = a<sup>2</sup> and x<sup>2</sup> + y<sup>2</sup> = b<sup>2</sup> (a > b > 0).
Evaluate ∬(x + y)<sup>2</sup> dx dy over the area bounded by the ellipse x<sup>2</sup>/a<sup>2</sup> + y<sup>2</sup>/b<sup>2</sup> = 1.
Evaluate ∬xy dx dy over the first quadrant of the circle x<sup>2</sup> + y<sup>2</sup> = a<sup>2</sup> (x ≥ 0, y ≥ 0).
Evaluate ∬y dx dy over the area bounded by the parabolas y<sup>2</sup> = 4x and x<sup>2</sup> = 4y.
Evaluate the triple integral ∭(x<sup>2</sup> + y<sup>2</sup> + z<sup>2</sup>) dx dy dz over the tetrahedral region bounded by x = 0, y = 0, z = 0 and x + y + z = a (a > 0).
Using triple integrals, find the volume of the tetrahedron bounded by the coordinate planes x = 0, y = 0, z = 0 and x + y + z = 1.
Trace the curve y<sup>2</sup>(a - x) = x<sup>2</sup>(a + x) by giving all its features in detail (symmetry, origin, tangents, asymptotes, and regions of existence).
Trace the Folium of Descartes / nodal curve x<sup>3</sup> + y<sup>3</sup> = a<sup>2</sup> x.

syllabus.head: Jacobians
syllabus.text: Definition, properties of Jacobians (J ·J' = 1, chain rule for Jacobians), Jacobian of implicit functions, transformation of coordinates.

syllabus.head: Approximation of Errors
syllabus.text: Partial differentials applied to approximation of errors, relative errors, and percentage errors in physical and engineering systems.

syllabus.head: Applications of Definite Integrals
syllabus.text: Evaluation of area of plane curves, length of curves (rectification), volumes and surface areas of solids of revolution (Cartesian, polar, and parametric forms).

syllabus.head: Centroids & Centers of Gravity
syllabus.text: Calculation of mass, first moments of area, center of gravity (CG), and center of mass of thin plates and laminae with variable density.

parts.text: If u<sup>3</sup> + v<sup>3</sup> + w<sup>3</sup> = x + y + z, u<sup>2</sup> + v<sup>2</sup> + w<sup>2</sup> = x<sup>3</sup> + y<sup>3</sup> + z<sup>3</sup>, and u + v + w = x<sup>2</sup> + y<sup>2</sup> + z<sup>2</sup>, find the Jacobian (∂(u, v, w))/(∂(x, y, z)).
If x + y + z = u, y + z = uv, z = uvw, show that the Jacobian (∂(x, y, z))/(∂(u, v, w)) = u<sup>2</sup> v.

Find the possible percentage error in computing the parallel resistance r of three resistances r<sub>1</sub>, r<sub>2</sub>, r<sub>3</sub> from the formula 1/r = 1/r<sub>1</sub> + 1/r<sub>2</sub> + 1/r<sub>3</sub>, if r<sub>1</sub>, r<sub>2</sub>, r<sub>3</sub> are each in error by +1.2%.
Find the volume and surface area generated by the revolution of the Astroid x = a cos<sup>3</sup>θ, y = a sin<sup>3</sup>θ about the x-axis.
Find the volume of the solid generated by revolving the semicircle x<sup>2</sup> + y<sup>2</sup> = a<sup>2</sup> (y ≥ 0) about the x-axis.
Find the volume generated when the loop of the curve y<sup>2</sup> = x<sup>2</sup>(x + 4) is revolved about the x-axis.
Find the area of the region bounded by the curves y = x and y = x<sup>2</sup> in the first quadrant using double integration.

pyqs.title: Mass and Center of Gravity of Lamina

parts.text: A triangular thin plate with vertices at (0, 0), (2, 0), and (2, 4) has a variable density ρ(x, y) = 1 + x + y. Find: (i) The total mass of the plate (M = ∬ρ dx dy). (ii) The position coordinates of its center of gravity (x̅, y̅).

syllabus.head: Vector Differentiation
syllabus.text: Scalar and vector point functions, vector differentiation, gradient of a scalar field, geometrical meaning of gradient, directional derivative, divergence and curl of vector fields, physical interpretations (solenoidal and irrotational fields), scalar potential functions.

syllabus.head: Vector Identities
syllabus.text: Laplacian operator (∇<sup>2</sup>), identities involving ∇(r<sup>n</sup>), ∇·(r⃗/r<sup>3</sup>), ∇ × (∇φ), ∇·(∇ × F⃗).

syllabus.head: Vector Integration
syllabus.text: Line integrals, surface integrals, volume integrals.

syllabus.head: Integral Theorems
syllabus.text: Gauss Divergence Theorem, Stokes' Theorem, and Green's Theorem in a plane (statements, verifications, and evaluations of flux and work done over bounded surfaces and volumes).

parts.text: Show that the vector field F⃗ = (r⃗)/(|r⃗|<sup>3</sup>) (where r⃗ = xî + yĵ + zk̂) is both irrotational and solenoidal. Find the scalar potential φ such that F⃗ = ∇φ.
A fluid motion is given by V⃗ = (y+z)î + (z+x)ĵ + (x+y)k̂. Show that the motion is irrotational and find its velocity potential.
Prove that the vector field F⃗ = (y<sup>2</sup> - z<sup>2</sup> + 3yz - 2x)î + (3xz + 2xy)ĵ + (3xy - 2xz + 2z)k̂ is solenoidal.
If F⃗ = x<sup>2</sup> yî - 2xzĵ + 2yzk̂, find div F⃗, curl F⃗, and curl(curl F⃗).
Find div F⃗ and curl F⃗ where F⃗ = ∇(x<sup>3</sup> + y<sup>3</sup> + z<sup>3</sup> - 3xyz).
If V⃗ = (xî + yĵ + zk̂)/(√(x<sup>2</sup> + y<sup>2</sup> + z<sup>2</sup>)), find the value of div V⃗.
Prove that div(grad r<sup>n</sup>) = ∇<sup>2</sup>(r<sup>n</sup>) = n(n+1)r<sup>n-2</sup>. Hence show that ∇<sup>2</sup>(1/r) = 0.
If u = x+y+z, v = x<sup>2</sup>+y<sup>2</sup>+z<sup>2</sup>, w = yz+zx+xy, prove that ∇u, ∇v, ∇w are coplanar vectors.
Find the directional derivative of φ(x, y, z) = x<sup>2</sup> yz + 4xz<sup>2</sup> at the point (1, -2, 1) in the direction of the vector 2î - ĵ - 2k̂.
Find the directional derivative of φ= (x<sup>2</sup> + y<sup>2</sup> + z<sup>2</sup>)<sup>-1/2</sup> at the point P(3, 1, 2) in the direction of the vector yzî + zxĵ + xyk̂.
Find the constants m and n such that the surface mx<sup>2</sup> - 2nyz = (m+4)x will be orthogonal to the surface 4x<sup>2</sup> y + z<sup>3</sup> = 4 at the point (1, -1, 2).

Apply Gauss Divergence Theorem to evaluate ∬<sub>S</sub> F⃗ ·n̂ dS, where F⃗ = 4x<sup>3</sup>î - x<sup>2</sup> yĵ + x<sup>2</sup> zk̂ and S is the surface of the cylinder x<sup>2</sup> + y<sup>2</sup> = a<sup>2</sup> bounded by planes z = 0 and z = b.

The vector field F⃗ = x<sup>2</sup>î + zĵ + yzk̂ is defined over the volume of the cuboid 0 ≤ x ≤ a, 0 ≤ y ≤ b, 0 ≤ z ≤ c enclosing surface S. Evaluate the surface integral ∬<sub>S</sub> F⃗ ·n̂ dS using Divergence Theorem.
State Gauss Divergence theorem. Verify it for F⃗ = 4xzî - y<sup>2</sup>ĵ + yzk̂ over the unit cube bounded by planes x = 0, x = 1, y = 0, y = 1, z = 0, z = 1.
Verify Stokes' Theorem for F⃗ = (x<sup>2</sup> + y<sup>2</sup>)î - 2xyĵ taken around the rectangle bounded by lines x = ±a, y = 0, and y = b.
Evaluate ∮<sub>C</sub> F⃗ ·dr⃗ by Stokes' Theorem, where F⃗ = y<sup>2</sup>î + x<sup>2</sup>ĵ - (x+z)k̂ and C is the boundary of the triangle with vertices (0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), and (1, 1, 0).

State Green's Theorem in a plane. Using it, evaluate ∮<sub>C</sub> (2x<sup>2</sup> - y<sup>2</sup>)dx + (x<sup>2</sup> + y<sup>2</sup>)dy, where C is the boundary of the area enclosed by the x-axis and upper half of the circle x<sup>2</sup> + y<sup>2</sup> = a<sup>2</sup>.
Verify Green's Theorem for ∮<sub>C</sub> {(3x<sup>2</sup> - 8y<sup>2</sup>)dx + (4y - 6xy)dy}, where C is the boundary of the triangular region bounded by x = 0, y = 0, and x + y = 1.
Using Green's Theorem, evaluate ∮<sub>C</sub> (x<sup>2</sup> y dx + x<sup>2</sup> dy) around the triangle with vertices (0, 0), (1, 0), (1, 1).
Verify Green's Theorem for ∮<sub>C</sub> (xy + y<sup>2</sup>)dx + x<sup>2</sup> dy over the boundary bounded by y = x and y = x<sup>2</sup>.

syllabus.head: Matrix Properties & Rank
syllabus.text: Matrix types, elementary row and column transformations, echelon form, normal canonical form ([I<sub>r</sub> |0]), rank of a matrix.

syllabus.head: System of Linear Equations
syllabus.text: Consistency of systems of non-homogeneous and homogeneous linear equations (AX = B and AX = 0), Rouché-Capelli theorem (rank(A) = rank[A |B]), conditions for unique, infinite, and no solutions.

syllabus.head: Eigenvalues & Eigenvectors
syllabus.text: Characteristic equation, roots, properties of eigenvalues, determination of eigenvectors, linear independence of eigenvectors.

syllabus.head: Cayley-Hamilton Theorem & Diagonalization
syllabus.text: Statement and verification of Cayley-Hamilton Theorem, computation of matrix inverse (A<sup>-1</sup>) and higher matrix powers (A<sup>4</sup>, A<sup>6</sup>), modal matrix (P), diagonalization of symmetric matrices (P<sup>-1</sup>AP = D).

syllabus.head: Vector Spaces & Subspaces
syllabus.text: Vector space axioms, subspaces, linear combinations, linear span, linear dependence and independence, basis and dimension, linear transformations.

parts.text: Reduce the matrix A = [2 3 -2 4; 3 -2 1 2; 3 2 3 4; -2 4 0 5] to normal form and find its rank.
Find the rank of the matrix A = [1 2 3 0; 2 4 3 2; 3 2 1 3; 6 8 7 5] using elementary row transformations.
Find the rank of the matrix A = [1 2 -1 4; 2 4 3 4; 1 2 3 4; -1 -2 6 -7] by reducing to normal form.
Find the rank of A = [1 2 3 2; 2 3 5 1; 1 3 4 5].

Test the consistency of the system of equations and solve if consistent: x<sub>1</sub> + 2x<sub>2</sub> - x<sub>3</sub> - 5x<sub>4</sub> = 4, x<sub>1</sub> + 3x<sub>2</sub> - 2x<sub>3</sub> - 7x<sub>4</sub> = 5, 2x<sub>1</sub> - x<sub>2</sub> + 3x<sub>3</sub> = 3.
Determine the values of λ and μ such that the system: 2x - 5y + 2z = 8, 2x + 4y + 6z = 5, x + 2y + λz = μ has: (i) No solution, (ii) A unique solution, (iii) Infinite number of solutions.
Find for what values of λ and μ the system: x + y + z = 16, x + 2y + 5z = 10, 2x + 3y + λz = μ has: (i) Unique solution, (ii) No solution, (iii) Infinite solutions. Solve for λ= 2, μ= 8.

Test consistency and solve: x<sub>1</sub> + 2x<sub>2</sub> - x<sub>3</sub> = 3, 3x<sub>1</sub> - x<sub>2</sub> + 2x<sub>3</sub> = 1, 2x<sub>1</sub> - 2x<sub>2</sub> + 3x<sub>3</sub> = 2, x<sub>1</sub> - x<sub>2</sub> + x<sub>3</sub> = -1.
Find the value of k (or λ) such that the homogeneous system has non-trivial solutions: 2x + 3y - 2z = 0, 3x - y + 3z = 0, 7x + ky - z = 0.
Find the eigenvalues and corresponding eigenvectors of the symmetric matrix: A = [-2 5 4; 5 7 5; 4 5 -2].
Calculate the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of the matrix A = [1 -6 -4; 0 4 2; 0 -6 -3].
Find the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of A = [3 1 4; 0 2 6; 0 0 5] and A = [6 -2 2; -2 3 -1; 2 -1 3].
Two eigenvalues of the matrix A = [-3 -7 -5; 2 4 3; 1 2 2] are 1 and 1. Find the third eigenvalue and find its corresponding eigenvector.
Prove that the eigenvalues of an upper triangular matrix are its diagonal elements.
For the matrix A = [1 2 -2; 1 2 1; -1 -1 0], find the modal matrix P and resulting diagonal matrix D.

Verify Cayley-Hamilton theorem for the matrix A = [2 -1 1; -1 2 -1; 1 -1 2]. Find A<sup>-1</sup> and evaluate A<sup>6</sup> - 6A<sup>5</sup> + 9A<sup>4</sup> - 2A<sup>3</sup> - 12A<sup>2</sup> + 23A - 9I.
Verify Cayley-Hamilton theorem for the matrix A = [4 3 1; 2 1 -2; 1 2 1] and compute A<sup>-1</sup>.
State Cayley-Hamilton theorem and verify it for A = [1 2; 2 4] and A = [1 4; 2 3].
Define subspace of a vector space. Show that the set W of all matrices of the form [a b; -b a] is a subspace of M<sub>22</sub>.
Define basis of a vector space. Show that the set of vectors {(1, 0, 0), (0, 1, 0), (0, 0, 1)} is a basis of R<sup>3</sup>.
Define a linear transformation. Show that T: R<sup>2</sup> → R<sup>3</sup> defined by T(x, y) = (x, 2x-y, 3x+4y) is a linear transformation.
Show that vectors (1, 3, 2), (1, -7, -8), (2, 1, -1) are linearly dependent in V<sub>3</sub>(F).
Prove that the intersection of any two subspaces of a vector space is also a subspace.
Let T: R<sup>3</sup> → R<sup>3</sup> be a linear transformation such that T(1, 0, 0) = (2, 4, -1), T(0, 1, 0) = (1, 3, -2), T(0, 0, 1) = (0, -2, 2). Compute T(-2, 4, -1).

labs.title: 3D Linear Transformation & Eigenvector Deformation Rig
points: Physical 3D Assets:
3D spatial coordinate grid displaying a unit sphere and canonical basis vectors î, ĵ, k̂.
Deformed ellipsoid visual mesh generated under linear transformation matrix A (Y = AX).
Interactive Controls:
Matrix Input Cells: Configurable 3 × 3 grid loading exam matrices (e.g., A = [-2 5 4; 5 7 5; 4 5 -2]).
Basis Vector Rotator: Rotates an arbitrary input vector X in 3D space.
Step-by-Step Echelon Stepper: Executes row operations live.
Real-Time Visual Mechanics:

Eigenvector Invariance: As vector X rotates, output vector AX generally changes direction; when X aligns with an eigenvector, AX stays collinear, scaling along the principal axis by eigenvalue factor λ.
Diagonalization / Modal Rotation: Transforms canonical axes into the orthogonal eigenvector basis, converting the full matrix A into pure uncoupled diagonal stretchings along axes.
Augmented Matrix Pivot Engine: Displays row operations on [A |B] step-by-step, highlighting zero rows to establish rank and identify consistent solution planes intersecting in 3D space.
